content: We become just by performing just acts, temperate by performing temperate acts, and brave by performing brave acts.
author: Aristotle
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

Across his life and work, Aristotle saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
